Design-only planning requested by Ryan during voice. Implementation remains unstarted; no code, infrastructure, deployment, purchase or publishing authorization is implied. Initial status stays open (Discovery), unassigned. As a publication operator, I want feeds and application delivery to reflect the same published content, so that visibility and updates are consistent across channels. Acceptance behavior (planned, not executable or verified yet): ```gherkin Feature: Share a published-content projection across public delivery channels Scenario: Publish, revise and withdraw an article Given a publication with a published article and a private newer draft When a reader requests its subscription feed or application representation Then both expose the same current published version and canonical identity And neither exposes the newer draft or private editorial data When a published revision or withdrawal is made Then both reflect that change within a documented freshness bound And an older delayed update cannot restore withdrawn or superseded public content Scenario: Keep publication boundaries Given two separately configured publications When public content is projected for one publication Then only that publication's eligible published content and public assets are included ``` Foundation dependency for both delivery epics. Later implementation must inspect and reuse the existing Published* lifecycle, ContentRepository, Markus/S3 projection and incremental reconciliation/invalidation behavior; do not build another publishing engine. Review current docs/public-surface.md, docs/site-hosting.md, projection/public_data.py and M8 PPY-f293ea. Existing latest/search JSON is not yet a versioned article-body delivery contract. Define explicit public field and asset allowlists; do not blindly expose metadata/frontMatterYaml or editorial internals. Define common eligibility, channel opt-outs, canonical IDs/URLs, published revision timestamps, withdrawal and cache/reconciliation behavior. Transport and hosting choices remain design work. Approved platform scope: whenever saving a content item changes publicly published content, automatically refresh its article representation, affected listings/indexes, sitemap, RSS and Atom, plus headless outputs when enabled. Publish, published edits and unpublish share the same content selection and metadata rules; private draft saves never enter public outputs. Failures of ancillary projections must be visible and retryable. Definition of Done includes the child post-save behavior story, published-only isolation, common identity/update selection and documented consistency/failure contracts. Orchestration, atomicity and transport details remain design decisions; no new services are prescribed. Promoted from story to epic solely to provide a schema-valid parent for the approved child behavior; ID, parent initiative, existing dependencies and implementation-unstarted status are preserved. Approved dependency design (supersedes any manual per-page predicate-configuration proposal): convention over configuration. Derive dependencies automatically from supported declarative listing/embedded-content constructs when the containing page is saved or compiled. The listing's existing selection parameters are the sole source of truth for rendering and invalidation; never ask editors to maintain a parallel per-page predicate file or separately copied rule. Generate a reverse index associating matching content with affected pages from those constructs. Initial predicate scope is item/issue type plus featured true, false or either; publication scope, published eligibility and existing authorization are separate enforced gates, never optional query filters. Multiple listing components on one page contribute the union of dependencies. A public content change refreshes pages whose derived selection matches either old OR new published state, covering new items, removals, unpublish and type/featured transitions, including candidates that can enter or displace a bounded listing. Saving/recompiling an edited listing page replaces its old registrations; deleting it removes stale reverse-index entries. Keep original ordering, limit and other supported selection semantics from the rendering construct rather than restating them for invalidation. Design questions remain: exact Markus versus Papyrus extension ownership, declarative construct/schema syntax and supported selection vocabulary; mapping current tag-based custom listings onto the proposed item/issue-type and featured semantics; index persistence/rebuild, freshness and failure handling; and a conservative fallback for unsupported custom dynamic queries. Do not claim generic arbitrary-Python/React/code analysis. No listing markup syntax is approved or asserted to exist by this plan. Orchestration and atomicity remain design choices; no new service is prescribed. Verified read-only source evidence, AnthusAI/Anth.us-web main 5ce142cab725cbf27e30ee15cb4904dc282da0d7 (not the older default develop/local checkout): web/anthus_pages.py homepage at line404 constructs the Recent posts section from posts[:3] image cards and posts[3:10] dated links; the output contains `
    {thumbs}
` and an optional `
    {posts_items}
`. These are Python-generated HTML fragments, not an authored Markus listing directive/node/plugin or runtime React listing. web/anthus_content.py:448 Collections.from_nodes selects published, non-folded, non-platform blog nodes tagged posts, ordered by descending date with source-name ties; this is not proof of a general item-type/featured construct. web/build_via_papyrus.py:470 generate_pages calls pages.homepage with collections, _generated at408 stores the fragment, and write_generated at704 wraps it with markus_shell.render_page directly, bypassing Markus body conversion. web/projector.py:369 Snapshot.inputs hashes each generated page title plus rewritten fragment, the sitemap bytes and public-data bytes; listing_inputs at557 exposes those digests to the existing incremental mechanism. Thus existing fragment-digest invalidation is a reuse candidate, but no construct-derived reverse index or generic dependency extraction is established by that source. Explicitly bridge the current custom-generator gap during design rather than inventing existing syntax or promising to infer arbitrary code. Source links: - https://github.com/AnthusAI/Anth.us-web/blob/5ce142cab725cbf27e30ee15cb4904dc282da0d7/web/anthus_pages.py#L404 - https://github.com/AnthusAI/Anth.us-web/blob/5ce142cab725cbf27e30ee15cb4904dc282da0d7/web/anthus_content.py#L448 - https://github.com/AnthusAI/Anth.us-web/blob/5ce142cab725cbf27e30ee15cb4904dc282da0d7/web/build_via_papyrus.py#L470 - https://github.com/AnthusAI/Anth.us-web/blob/5ce142cab725cbf27e30ee15cb4904dc282da0d7/web/build_via_papyrus.py#L704 - https://github.com/AnthusAI/Anth.us-web/blob/5ce142cab725cbf27e30ee15cb4904dc282da0d7/web/projector.py#L369 This inspection establishes source behavior, not a fresh live-deployment audit. Existing M3 PPY-3d905d work is preserved; implementation remains unstarted for this extension.

Shared behavior records: PPY-c08790af-4c51-4c9d-a7ae-7a3346504bb2 (one path-based page/content system), PPY-b6ede164-fad8-45da-a242-51362c5f8285 (authored homepage composition with reusable listings). Migration design task: PPY-d16f6481-3a24-4438-94cb-ac6ed8ef34e7. Help/wiki and ordinary site pages share this foundation and its construct-derived index/post-save refresh; neither wiki navigation nor product theming creates an independent content engine.
